% Files of the document named like .4ht files that TeX's tree also has:
% report.ltx after \documentclass{report}, dvipsnam.ltx before
% \usepackage[dvipsnames]{xcolor}, which reads dvipsnam.def, and latin1.ltx
% before \usepackage[latin1]{inputenc}, which reads latin1.def. As in the
% PDF, each file's text is in the page, the chapter keeps report's form,
% a named color keeps its value, and the degree sign is set as latin1.4ht
% sets it.
\documentclass{report}
\input{report.ltx}
\input{dvipsnam.ltx}
\usepackage[dvipsnames]{xcolor}
\input{latin1.ltx}
\usepackage[latin1]{inputenc}
\begin{document}
\chapter{Files}
Report: \ownreport

Dvipsnam: \owndvipsnam

\textcolor{BrickRed}{Brick red text.}

Latin1: \ownlatin

An angle of 30\textdegree.
\end{document}
